parsed.explanation: The parent national regime governs every arrival: sex-as-assigned-at-birth markers, refusal to process X markers, document-discrepancy refusals, possible lifetime fraud findings, reported passport confiscations and stranded travellers, plus allied-government advisories. National immigration custody carries documented severe harm to trans detainees (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse), with challenges unresolved. This state/province itself is genuinely protective: no bathroom/facility ban, 2013 gender-identity anti-discrimination covering public accommodations, hate-crime penalty enhancement, marker change on provider affidavit, and a July 2026 national assessment places it in the Low-Risk group. But local protections operate only after entry and cannot displace the border/document regime or national custody conditions. The exposure is a known traveller-facing universal measure with severe detention outcomes and no working remedy, not organised street-level targeting or near-certain imprisonment, so it sits in the Elevated Risk band rather than lower.
